 Get a glimpse of the Hunter's Moon and Saturn tonight in Philly region's sky 
 Although it is close to Halloween, there is no indication that werewolves will be present Sunday night. 
 By Justin Godynick and Brendan Brightman • 
 Published October 25, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 25, 2026 at 7:45 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 The chill will remain, but you can get a great view of the Harvest Moon and Saturn Sunday night. NBC10 First Alert Meteorologist Justin Godynick has the full forecast. 
 Sunday night will be special for stargazers because the Hunter's Moon and Saturn will be viewable for us Earthlings. 
 Thankfully, skies will be clear for the viewing . 
 Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
   WATCH HERE 
 View this post on Instagram 
 To get a glimpse of the Hunter's Moon, look east toward the sunset. Views will peak at around midnight. 
 For Saturn, look below and left of the moon.
 View this post on Instagram 
 What is the Hunter's Moon?
 The Hunter's Moon is the name for October's full moon. It is believed to have gotten its name because it signaled the time for humans to go hunting before the winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac .
 NBC10 Xfinity Cam NBC10 Xfinity Cam Taken at around 8:54 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 25. 
 "Following the Harvest Moon, fields are typically cleared, leaves have fallen, and animals are easier to spot in open landscapes. At the same time, game such as deer and other wildlife have fattened up over the summer and early fall, making this an ideal time for hunting," according to the Almanac.
